subject: FU-1: Daemon singleton guard — stop zombie daemon pile-up on :8787 (HIGH)
description:
Fix the root cause of the outage during the codex-parity session (see note-mqgw7oy7b8z). The daemon has NO singleton/liveness guard on boot: repeated MCP self-boots / start-daemon hooks accumulate multiple `node daemon.js` instances fighting over port 8787. One wedges (holds the LISTEN socket but stops answering GET /ping), and fresh spawns log "port 8787 busy (predecessor draining?)" 30× then exit, leaving the wedged holder in place — daemon down and not self-recovering. Recovery required manually killing all daemon.js PIDs and starting one clean instance.

Implement a boot-time guard in daemon.js (and align hooks/start-daemon.js + hooks/start-daemon.sh): before binding, if a HEALTHY daemon already answers GET /ping within a short timeout, exit 0 (do not spawn a duplicate); if a process owns the port but is UNHEALTHY (no /ping response), reap it (or fail loudly, surfacing the offending PID) before binding rather than retry-then-exit. Consider a pidfile + liveness check. Add a test simulating a wedged holder (port held, /ping non-responsive) and assert the new daemon either reaps-and-binds or exits cleanly without leaving a wedged process. Files: daemon.js, hooks/start-daemon.js, hooks/start-daemon.sh. Severity: HIGH — caused a live outage, will recur.
